description: We are a team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge working on The Earth Information Jukebox challenge! Our goal is to transform NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) visual data into rich, real-time dynamic sonifications—making complex Earth science accessible, engaging, and multi-sensory for everyone.
summary:
AEVYRA is an interactive Earth sonification platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into meaningful sound, allowing people to hear, explore, and understand our planet’s changing environment.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge’s Earth Jukebox challenge, AEVYRA combines satellite imagery, machine learning, and data-driven sound mapping to translate environmental patterns into immersive audio experiences. Users can explore changes in nighttime lights, temperature, CO₂, and aerosols across different years and geographic regions.

The platform features data-based audio layering, allowing users to isolate and explore individual environmental variables, alongside spatial audio that represents geographic differences. It also incorporates vibration-based feedback, screen reader compatibility, and keyboard navigation to make Earth science more accessible, including for people with visual impairments.

By combining scientific data, sound, and inclusive interaction, AEVYRA goes beyond traditional visualizations. It makes complex environmental changes easier to perceive, compare, and understand, helping people connect with Earth's evolving story through multiple senses.
details:
AEVYRA – Hear the Earth. Feel the Change.

Project Overview

AEVYRA is an interactive, multisensory Earth exploration platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Earth Jukebox challenge. It transforms NASA Earth observation imagery and environmental data into meaningful sound, allowing people to hear and explore changes happening across our planet.

Traditional Earth observation platforms rely heavily on maps, graphs, and visualizations. While scientifically valuable, these methods can be difficult for non-experts to interpret and less accessible to people with visual impairments. AEVYRA addresses this by introducing sound, spatial interaction, and vibration as alternative ways to experience environmental information.

How AEVYRA Works

AEVYRA follows a data-driven sonification process that connects environmental information with sound.

1. Earth Observation Data

The platform uses NASA Earth observation resources to explore environmental patterns, including nighttime lights, temperature, atmospheric CO₂, and aerosols. Users can select different datasets, years, and geographic regions to investigate how Earth's conditions change over time.

2. Image Analysis and Machine Learning

Satellite imagery is processed using Python-based image analysis and machine learning techniques, including K-means clustering, to identify meaningful visual patterns and extract numerical features.

These extracted features are organized into structured JSON data, providing the connection between the scientific analysis and the interactive web application.

3. Data-to-Sound Mapping

AEVYRA translates environmental features into sound using defined sonification rules. Parameters such as pitch, rhythm, intensity, and timbre are controlled by changes in the underlying data rather than being assigned randomly.

Using Tone.js, the platform generates sound experiences that reflect differences between environmental conditions. The mapping is designed to balance scientific meaning with musicality, making the results informative while remaining engaging and comfortable to listen to.

4. Data Layering and Spatial Exploration

One of AEVYRA's key features is its data-based layering system. Rather than simply separating audio by musical instrument, users can explore meaningful environmental components individually and understand how they contribute to the overall sound.

Spatial audio further enhances the experience by representing geographic differences through sound, connecting the listening experience with the selected Earth region.

5. Interactive Exploration

Through the web interface, users can explore Earth observation imagery, select years and geographic regions, listen to generated sound, and compare changing environmental patterns.

The interface combines an interactive globe, satellite imagery, environmental indicators, and a dedicated sound player to create an engaging Earth exploration experience.

Accessibility and Inclusive Design

Accessibility is a central consideration in AEVYRA's design.

The platform incorporates:

  • Vibration-based feedback: An additional sensory channel for communicating environmental changes on supported devices.
  • Screen reader compatibility: Helps users with visual impairments navigate and understand the interface.
  • Keyboard navigation: Allows users to interact with the platform without relying on a mouse.
  • Spatial audio: Provides an additional way to perceive differences across geographic areas.
  • Data-based audio layers: Gives users greater control over the information they want to explore.

These features aim to make Earth observation data more inclusive, particularly for people who face barriers when using conventional visual dashboards.

Technologies Used

AEVYRA combines web development, machine learning, scientific data processing, and audio synthesis.

  • React and JavaScript: Interactive frontend development.
  • Python: Satellite image processing, feature extraction, and machine learning.
  • K-means clustering: Identifying patterns within Earth observation imagery.
  • JSON: Transferring processed environmental information and sound-mapping parameters to the frontend.
  • Tone.js: Real-time, browser-based audio synthesis and playback.
  • NASA Earth observation resources: Scientific imagery and environmental datasets used to create the Earth stories.

AI Assistance and Data Transparency

Parts of the application code and data-processing scripts were developed with AI assistance. All environmental data values used by AEVYRA are derived from NASA imagery through the project's documented image-processing and feature-extraction methodology.

AI assistance was used to support development, while the scientific inputs and data-to-sound relationships remain grounded in the processed NASA imagery.

Creativity and Innovation

AEVYRA approaches Earth science communication through a combination of scientific analysis, interactive storytelling, and multisensory experience.

Instead of treating sonification as background music, the platform connects changes in environmental information to corresponding changes in sound.

Its data-based layering system makes it possible to investigate different environmental characteristics individually, while spatial audio and vibration introduce additional ways to perceive the information.

The combination of machine learning, data-driven sound mapping, interactive visualization, and accessibility-focused design creates an alternative to conventional Earth observation dashboards.

Intended Impact

AEVYRA aims to make Earth science more approachable, engaging, and accessible to a wider audience.

By transforming complex environmental patterns into interactive sound experiences, it encourages users to explore environmental changes, compare observations across time and space, and develop a deeper understanding of our changing planet.

The project also demonstrates how sonification and inclusive design can complement traditional scientific visualizations, creating new opportunities for environmental education, public awareness, and accessible data exploration.

AEVYRA invites everyone to experience Earth's story beyond what they can see — to hear the Earth and feel the change.
